item.title: Warriors owner admits Yaxel Lendeborg has changed his thoughts on making trades
item.description: Warriors owner admits Yaxel Lendeborg has changed his thoughts on making trades originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It's been a very impressive start to the season for Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. There was a lot of hope that Lendeborg was going to be this type of player when the Warriors drafted him in the first round, though there were also some concerns about him not being this because of his age. Ultimately, the Warriors didn't worry too much about his age and decided to go get the player who they thought was the best available at the time. Right now, there's a strong argument that Lendeborg is the best rookie in the NBA. It's also fair to mention that the Warriors' window could be extended because of how he looks. Stephen Curry is only getting older, and that's a problem for the Warriors trying to compete for the next decade, as he's 38 years old and only has a few seasons left, but it does help the team make some decisions on trying to compete right now. With Curry playing at this level, averaging a ridiculous 30 points per game at his age, including shooting 42.9% from 3-point range, and Lendeborg averaging 21.5 points and proving that he's a serviceable player on both sides of the floor, it could cause the Warriors to go out and make the necessary moves to improve over the next couple of months. According to Golden State's owner, it changes the outlook of how the team is going to make decisions over the next couple of months. “We got this one right. I was 100% sold that this was the guy we wanted in the draft. This guy is the real deal. Yeah, it changes our outlook about what we might wanna do,” owner Joe Lacob said, H/T Heavy . The Warriors are in a position to make a move or two, but it won't be easy because of limited assets. The Warriors do have a couple of players they could deal, but it doesn't always feel like they're in a position to make a blockbuster deal with the assets they have. Lendeborg and Curry together, if they can continue playing at this level and bring in a third guy, could be all the team needs, however. item.title: Pleasant volleyball dominates again in OHSAA regional with Centerburg
item.description: ONTARIO — The Spartans continue to stick to the script. For the 26th time in 26 matches in 2026, Pleasant's volleyball team won a 3-0 match, this time beating Centerburg 25-12, 25-10, 25-16 during a Division V regional semifinal Nov. 4 in the O-rena at Ontario High School. Pleasant, ranked No. 7 in the state coaches poll for D-V, will face top-ranked Coldwater at 2 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 7 back in the O-rena. The Cavaliers (22-4) also posted a 3-0 win, topping No. 3 Huron (22-4) by scores of 25-16, 29-27, 25-13. "They just keep gaining the momentum and the confidence, and I think they want it so badly that they aren’t even willing to let a point go. I love it," Pleasant coach Kory Ute said of her team. Pleasant was never threatened In a season of dominance, it might have been the most dialed-in performance of the season by the Spartans (26-0). "This is definitely the best we’ve played skill-wise. We had so much energy. We were very honed in in what we were doing," Pleasant senior defensive specialist Siri Veladanda said. "We all know this is the time of season where you can’t afford to make small mistakes. This is when you need to hone those skills. We knew that coming into this game." Back at the O-rena, site of their closest set of the season when the Warriors scored 22 points in a 25-22 third-set loss, Pleasant didn't leave anything to chance. The longest run they've allowed this season was five points at Ontario, but against Centerburg (23-3), they only allowed the Trojans to peel off a 3-point run. And with the exception of 1-0 to start the second set, the Spartans never trailed Wednesday night. "It was the first thing we said when we were watching film. We’ve got to make sure we establish what we can do and do it quickly so they know," Ute said. "I don’t want another team having any hope. I don’t want them thinking they are going to be part of the game." item.description: The tour of dangerous Big 12 quarterbacks continues for the Cincinnati Bearcats as they visit No. 17 Houston on Saturday afternoon, Nov. 7, at TDECU Stadium. The Bearcats have faced the scrambling abilities of Kansas State 's Avery Johnson, the passing threat of Arizona's Noah Fifita, the unpredictability of West Virginia's Michael Hawkins Jr., Texas Tech's Will Hammond and Utah's dual-threat Devon Dampier. The Big 12 wins came against Kansas State with Johnson and Texas Tech with Hammond , while the escapability of Fifita, Hawkins and Dampier led to three Big 12 losses . Next up is Houston's Conner Weigman, who was at Texas A&M two seasons ago. The 6-foot-3 native Texan is No. 14 in the nation in passing efficiency, ahead of Hawkins and Dampier, who gave UC fits. He is No. 8 in passing touchdowns with 20, more than Fifita and Dampier and seven more than UC's JC French IV. He's No. 20 in passing yards with 2,053, more than Dampier, who lit the Bearcats up for three passing touchdowns. "Weigman does everything really, really good," UC Bearcats coach Scott Satterfield said. "He can make all the throws, he's sneaky fast, he can make safeties miss when he runs the football. They run the offense through him. He's the catalyst for their offense. They don't ever get themselves out of position." Houston leads the nation in third-down efficiency at 60%, compared to UC at No. 33 at 44.6%. Cincinnati Bearcats vs. Houston Cougars football history It's all even, 15-15, but the Bearcats have won five straight. UC shut the Cougars out 34-0 in 2024 , the first year for current coach Willie Fritz. The game before that in 2023 was in Houston, where the Bearcats recorded their first Big 12 win, 24-14 against the Dana Holgorsen-coached Cougars . Houston's last win came at Nippert Stadium in 2016 as the Cougars rolled Tommy Tuberville's last UC team, 40-16. item.title: Yankees get big update on 39 home run slugger to replace Ryan McMahon
item.description: Yankees get big update on 39 home run slugger to replace Ryan McMahon originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees have a strong case for being the most interesting team in Major League Baseball to watch this offseason, though it's going to be a lot different than usual because of the expected lockout at the beginning of December. With the Yankees having some time to make moves prior to that, landing a guy like Teruaki Sato prior to the lockout, with his posting window being just 45 days, could put New York in a very strong position to make some moves after the lockout finishes. According to the latest report from Ken Rosenthal, there's a sense that the Yankees could use him at third base, but he also has the possibility to play another infield position, and he expects the Yankees to be a fit and involved in his market. “The Yankees probably could use him most at third base,” Rosenthal said , H/T NJ.com. “Ryan McMahon has one more year on his contract and they could easily replace him and maybe send him somewhere else, do something else with him. So [Sato] is a fit, I expect the Yankees to be involved in the Sato market.” Sato is going to have the same type of questions that guys like Munetaka Murakami had coming over to America, and a lot of that is just focused on the difference in competition between the NPB and Major League Baseball. However, all he did was swing it at a ridiculous level during his time in Japan, so there's no reason to believe that he's going to come to America and struggle. In 2026, he slashed .306/.383/.609 with a ridiculous 39 home runs and 106 RBIs. item.title: There’s one team the 49ers should trade Mac Jones to, and it’s because they’d overpay
item.description: There’s one team the 49ers should trade Mac Jones to, and it’s because they’d overpay originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco 49ers are perhaps the most interesting team to watch at this year's NFL trade deadline, and that includes possibly moving on from a guy like Mac Jones. While most of the focus for the 49ers will be on who they can bring in, there's an argument that trading Jones could actually help them do that. Moving on from Jones could mean a deal that brings in a player who improves their defense or wide receiving corps, while the assets they get in return could be used in another trade. Regardless, there's no debate that trading Jones could have some benefits. Reports have continued to indicate there's little chance it'll happen because Kyle Shanahan really likes him as a player, and he understands that if Brock Purdy gets injured, he wants a guy he can trust. Despite that reality, The Athletic once again raised him as a potential option, with the Minnesota Vikings as the team that could benefit from trading for him. “This one is a stretch, but bear with me. Despite Kyler Murray being close to a breakthrough — he’s still in the early stages of Kevin O’Connell’s offense — what if he has another unproductive game in Week 8 and the Vikings brass gets nervous? Murray is on a one-year deal, and they didn’t invest much to get him. “Jones is another former first-round pick who already has a year of Shanahan rehabbing under his belt and has shown he could play at a relatively high level in the right environment,” Ted Nguyen wrote . The Vikings have been one of the better teams in the NFL this season, and a lot of it is because of what they're able to do on the defensive side of the football. The offense has been very stagnant for most of the year, to say the least. It's also important to recognize, however, that Kyler Murray has dealt with some injuries and is still trying to figure out the rest of this offense. That takes time, which could result in the Vikings wanting to give him more of an opportunity. item.title: Yankees news: Shelley Duncan defects for job with Red Sox
item.description: TAMPA, FL - FEBRUARY 28: Shelley Duncan of the New York Yankees poses for a portrait during the New York Yankees Photo Day at George M. Steinbrenner Field on February 28, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by New York Yankees/Getty Images) | Getty Images NY Daily News | Gary Phillips: The Yankees’ organization lost one of the cogs of their farm system on Wednesday, as news broke that their Triple-A manager Shelley Duncan had accepted a job with the Boston Red Sox to join their major league staff. Duncan has been the skipper of the RailRiders for the past four seasons, earning International League Manager of the Year honors in 2025, and oversaw the leap of several key faces on the current Yankees’ roster from fringe prospects to outright stardom in the case of Ben Rice and Cam Schlittler. With his contract expiring though, Duncan was free to explore new roles and he found a decent promotion landing in Boston. Duncan’s new role on the Red Sox is still to be determined, though based on the gaps on their staff it is likely that he’ll serve as either their first or third base coach. MLB.com | Sam Dykstra: The Arizona Fall League is nearing the end of its run, and the Fall Stars Game is set to kick off this weekend on Sunday. The game features plenty of blue chip prospects, and last year’s class saw some names that immediately made an impression the next year in MLB. Ten of MLB Pipeline’s Top 100 Prospects will be on the field, and the Yankees will have one of them as Dax Kilby will get an invite to the game after he posted a .980 OPS in 15 games thus far. Chris Veach will join Kilby as the other Yankees representative at the game, the pitcher having tossed 9.2 innings in six appearances with a 3.72 ERA. FanGraphs | Jay Jaffe: A few days ago the ballot for the Hall of Fame Era Committee came out, and as Nick outlined for us , there were a number of people with Yankees ties up for election. Jaffe is working his way through the cases for each candidate, and his latest stop took him to Lou Piniella’s career. Sweet Lou came oh-so-close to election in previous ballots, but a stacked crowd this time around and a career that weighs heavily on his longevity rather than triumph beyond his early days managing in Cincinnati could hold him back from enshrinement.

item.title: A Surprisingly Dominant Relief Campaign
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CA - OCTOBER 06: Yuki Matsui #1 of the San Diego Padres celebrates as he leaves the field during Game Three of the National League Division Series presented by Booking.com between the Milwaukee Brewers and the San Diego Padres at Petco Park on Tuesday, October 6, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Rob Tringali/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Yuki Matsui The Padres signed Matsui to a five-year, $28 million deal heading into the 2024 season after the left-hander became an international free agent. He was the first free agent they signed that offseason to bolster their pitching staff after dealing away superstar Juan Soto to the New York Yankees. Matsui gave them modest results in 2024 and ‘25, posting sub-4.00 ERAs over 60-plus innings in both years. Overall Grade: A+ He took that to new heights in 2026. Matsui posted a blistering 1.83 ERA and .171 opponent batting average across 64 innings of work. Since coming over from Japan, Matsui has struggled with command (1.22 career WHIP). In spite of that, he managed to work out of jams in 2026, regularly recording outs in key situations. Matsui was especially dominant down the stretch with a 1.42 ERA in his final 30 appearances and a 0.68 ERA in his last 15 outings. Some of that may have been due to luck. Matsui’s expected ERA (3.03) was more than a full run above his actual mark (1.83). However, his expected opponent batting average (.170) was almost the exact same as his actual, so it’s hard to make heads or tells of it. Fielding Independent Pitching (FIP) is a metric used to determine how dominant a pitcher is on his own (using homers, walks, hit-by-pitches and strikeouts). Essentially, it measures how good a pitcher is without his defense. Matsui’s 4.18 FIP isn’t exactly sterling, so the defense may have had something to do with it. All that said, his season with the Friars was incredible. Matsui surprised just about everyone by being one of the most dominant left-handed relievers in the game. He was even better than his teammate Adrian Morejon (though he certainly doesn’t have the same track record as Morejon). Matsui decided earlier this week to remain with the Padres for the 2027 season, choosing not to exercise his opt-out. He’ll fill an important role in the Padres’ bullpen with the potential departures of Morejon and Jason Adam on the rise.

item.title: 2026 Atlanta Braves Player Review: Austin Wynns
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JUNE 12: Austin Wynns #16 of the Atlanta Braves looks on during the second inning of the game against the New York Mets at Citi Field on June 12, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Dustin Satloff/Getty Images) | Getty Images A serious bout of catcher injuries struck the Atlanta Braves during the first half of the season, and desperate times called for desperate measures. One of those measures, of the band-aid variety, ended up being Austin Wynns, who spent two weeks with the club in June and appeared in six games. How Acquired The Braves added Wynns in the middle of the season, while both Drake Baldwin and Sean Murphy were down with injuries. They sent cash considerations to the Angels in exchange for Wynns’ services, and designated longtime third-string catcher Chadwick Tromp in a corresponding move. The reasoning was a bit weird, though it was all meant to be a temporary fix anyway: Sandy Leon was getting the bulk of playing time anyway, so the Braves opted to acquire a backup-to-Leon instead of using Tromp in that role for whatever reason. One silly thing about the Wynns acquisition is that the Braves kind of prompted it with their own DFA of Jonah Heim earlier in the season. The Athletics, who acquired Wynns in a midseason trade in 2025, DFAed him three days after trading for Heim. He was released and signed with the Angels, but didn’t get promoted to their big league team. Three weeks later, the Braves traded cash considerations (which is what they received for Heim) to Anaheim for Wynns. What were the expectations? There weren’t any real expectations, to be blunt. Coming into 2026, the 35-year-old Wynns had a career 74 wRC+ that featured a pretty sizable xwOBA overperformance (.282 wOBA, .265 xwOBA) in 783 career PAs spanning parts of six major league seasons. He had never topped 180 PAs in a single season, nor 1.0 fWAR. He came kind of close in 2025 riding a massive xwOBA overperformance (.365 wOBA, .295 xwOBA), though. He also wasn’t highly regarded defensively, with just one good defensive year (2023) behind the plate and some substantially below-average performance in other seasons. He wasn’t doing much of anything in 2026, either — a -47 wRC+ (yes, a negative sign) in 43 PAs in Sacramento before getting released. Basically, the Braves acquired a guy who had 0.6 career fWAR in 826 PAs at the big league level. item.title: River View volleyball pillaged by Pirates in another bitter Sweet 16
item.description: LOGAN — River View has the luxury of a senior class with three previous regional tournament trips to its credit, but that proved to offer little in the way of an advantage in 2026. The Black Bears' hitters were error-plagued and struggled equally to adjust to Wheelersburg’s moving blocks and aggressive defensive coverage in a 25-18, 25-22, 25-17 loss in a Division IV regional semifinal loss at Jim Myers Gymnasium. The Lady Bears (24-2) fell a win short of the Elite Eight for the fourth straight season, even as a senior-laden team made significant defensive improvements from the past three seasons. It was that scrappy play on the back end from the likes of junior Kelsie Smith and junior libero Lindyn Fry that saved points and prolonged several extended rallies between the teams, particularly in the first two sets. They had 39 digs — an average of 13 per set — between them. In the end, though, a multitude of hitting errors against the Pirates’ blockers proved the difference. Seven came in the second set after River View took a 16-12 lead and appeared to have found some rhythm. River View coach Rose Olinger said an effective block “gets in your head after a while” and can have a negative impact on a hitter’s general confidence. On this occasion, it was the lack of conversions on pin attacks that provided the most problems for the offense. Most of their success came from middle hitters Avie Wright and Remi Lewis. That, of course, had much to do with the Pirates’ scrappy defensive play, which Olinger said wasn’t something they saw during scouting. “Their defense backed their blockers better than I anticipated,” Olinger said. “But I knew their block would be tough to get past.” Despite the loss, the team overall enjoyed one the program’s best overall seasons. Their 24 wins was the most in the Olinger era, and the win against Meadowbrook in the regular season finale was arguably the biggest under her watch as a coach. Smith, a record-setting setter who will sign with Marist next week, was part of a senior class that approached 100 wins in four years with four district titles. This year, the Lady Bears bagged another Muskingum Valley League-Big School title, despite losing all-time kills leader Haley Balo, now at Ashland, to graduation. Olinger tried to keep those feelings in perspective after another painstaking regional loss, one that saw daughter Layla play her final game. “It's a special group,” Olinger said. “The seniors, they're definitely leaving a legacy, but the whole team, this whole group, is just a special group.” Smith added 29 assists to her all-team career and single-season record, while Remi Lewis led the hitters with 10 kills and Avie Wright contributed eight. Jozie Adams, a freshman, had six on the outside to go with 12 digs. Wheelersburg (22-3), which was ousted by eventual state runner-up New Lexington in last year’s Division V regional semifinal, will play unbeaten, fourth-ranked Gallipolis Gallia Academy for a state berth at 4 p.m.

item.title: Rams cornerback Jaylen Watson to undergo season-ending shoulder surgery as injuries continue to mount
item.description: Los Angeles Rams cornerback Jaylen Watson (35) celebrates an interception during an NFL football game against the Buffalo Bills on October 12, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, CA. LOS ANGELES — The Los Angeles Rams suffered another significant blow to their injury-riddled roster Wednesday when head coach Sean McVay announced that cornerback Jaylen Watson will undergo season-ending shoulder surgery, leaving the team without one of its most productive defensive players. Watson had been attempting to play through the injury, but after consulting with doctors, the Rams determined that surgery was the best course of action rather than risk further damage. He will be placed on injured reserve and is expected to return next season. "That's a big one, bummer for him," McVay said Wednesday. "He's been such a stud for us. He wanted to be able to play through it, just understanding the totality of it all and just some of the different things, recommended to be able to get that surgery and that'll put them on IR for the year, but he's been awesome. Whenever he gets back next year, we'll be better." McVay said the risk of Watson aggravating the injury was too significant to allow him to continue playing. Although the shoulder could have been stabilized with additional support, doing so would have restricted his movement and potentially compromised his effectiveness. "The likelihood of it coming out and doing further damage to it is a very high probability," McVay said. "You could strap it, but it would restrict his movement. Just some of the different things that we've received from our doctors, it's the right thing to do by him, even though it sucks because he's been such a bright spot for us." Watson's absence creates another challenge for a Rams defense that has already dealt with injuries throughout the season. McVay praised the cornerback's toughness, leadership and willingness to play through pain, recalling a moment during the team's Week 7 game against the Las Vegas Raiders when Watson was receiving intravenous fluids because of cramping. "A couple of weeks ago, he's cramping at the Raiders game and he says when he's getting an IV, 'Give me half a bag. I need to get back out there,'" McVay said. "He's been awesome. He's been playing through some different stuff, but he's been really productive and it's unfortunate that that happened." item.description: (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich has been battered by injuries—there is no denying it. Yes, the squad is stretched thinner than anyone would like. And yes, having half the medical department on speed dial is not exactly ideal preparation for a Champions League showdow n—but welcome to Atlético Madrid. Nobody is handing out sympathy points at the Metropolitano. Diego Simeone is not going to look at Bayern Munich’s injury report and politely agree to make things easier or offer to let the Bavarians borrow a few subs. Atlético Madrid will press, scrap, frustrate, kick, counter, and generally make ninety minutes feel like an appointment with the dentist. They will smell vulnerability, and Bayern Munich cannot afford to show any. This is precisely the kind of match that separates a talented team from a genuinely resilient one. Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano, Jos hua Kimmich, and the rest of the available squad need to show some leadership. The youngsters and squad players need to embrace their opportunities rather than look around wondering who is missing. Bayern Munich has had two consecutive Champions League draws, a bruising injury situation, and plenty of reasons to feel sorry for themselves (though, credit to them, they have not gone down that road). Enough. This is gut-check time. No perfect lineup, no ideal circumstances, and absolute ly no sympathy from Simeone. Just Bayern Munich against one of Europe’s most uncomfortable opponents. It is time for Bayern Munich to roll up its sleeves and remind everyone what this team is made of. While not an absolute expert on their music, there are plenty of good sings produced by the group since their inception that you absolutely cannot avoid on the radio here in the United States. One that I actually think gets underplayed is “DOA”, which I rank as the best of its modern era. item.title: Colts Have 1 Overlooked Trade Chip Hardly Anyone Is Talking About
item.description: Bills named as potential fit for Keenan Allen. Getty The Indianapolis Colts are selling right now and have already dealt Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. It would be shocking if they stop there as there have already been plenty of rumors about the Colts potentially trading running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs. Both of them are rightfully drawing the headlines but one player who is not being talked about as much is Keenan Allen. The 34-year-old has 36 receptions for 325 yards and one touchdown on the season. He had a DUI in September which was not a great look but to his credit he has shown up and played well for Indianapolis this season. There are plenty of teams across the NFL who could use a veteran wide receiver so the Colts should be in a pretty advantageous position. A team like the San Francisco 49ers would make a lot of sense since they have dealt with injuries to basically their entire wide receiver room and could use some insurance at the position especially if Mike Evans went down with a major injury at some point. Deebo Samuel has also been banged up. The Los Angeles Rams lost DaVante Adams who will likely be out for a good chunk of the rest of the regular season so Allen would be a nice veteran fill-in who could give quarterback Matthew Stafford another weapon and could take a little pressure off Puka Nacua. To stay on the NFC West theme, the Seattle Seahawks are another team that could use a receiver. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is incredible but he cannot carry the load for that offense all on his own. Allen would at least give that offense another guy to turn to. The Kansas City Chiefs could also factor into the mix since they have been linked to other receivers who might be traded like Brian Thomas Jr. so if they are unable to land someone like him then Allen could be a backup option. Colts should be patient with Keenan Allen The Colts are in a good position with Allen. They don’t have to rush ahead of the November 10 trade deadline even though they may be taking a risk that he gets hurt in the team’s game the Sunday before the deadline but if they wait and other receivers start to go off the board then desperate teams may turn to the Colts and start asking about Allen. They probably won’t be able to get more than a fifth round draft pick for him, and that’s in a best-case scenario, but for a rebuilding team like the Colts they need all the draft picks they can get so while he isn’t as big of a chip as Taylor or Downs the Colts should be shopping him. Green Bay Packers star running back Josh Jacobs seems confident that he will not miss any action the rest of the way despite new allegations of physical and verbal abuse from three women . item.title: Amity shuts out Hand, wins SCC girls soccer title after 20-year championship drought
item.description: Amity Regional players celebrate after defeating Daniel Hand 6-0 in the SCC Girls Soccer Final at West Haven High School in West Haven, Conn., Wednesday, November 4, 2026. (Dave Zajac/Hearst Connecticut Media) WEST HAVEN - The Amity girls soccer team got through the gauntlet that is the SCC unbeaten during the regular season. Then the Spartans added three more victories in the league tournament, including a 6-0 blitz of Hand in the final Wednesday night at Ken Strong Stadium. The feat was impressive for the Spartans (15-1-3), even with the three ties. They were able to accomplish it without Maggie Kershnar, a 2025 GametimeCT First Team All-State selection who is out for the season due to a knee injury. Kershnar will play at UConn next season. It also included three wins over Mercy, a team that has had plenty of success in the SCC this decade. "We knew we were the No. 1 seed and we had to perform like the No. 1 seed and tonight, we did," Amity girls soccer coach Owen Quigley said. "We didn't give Hand a chance to settle on the ball tonight." Olivia Huber had two goals and two assists to earn the SCC Tournament's Most Outstanding Player award and lead the way for Amity, which won its first SCC championship since 2006. "I feel like that's something we've really focused on this season, trying to be the first team to score because that really kind of dictates the rest of the game," Huber said. Quigley was at Amity for that 2006 title - a win over Mercy - and the Spartans went on to share the Class LL title with Trumbull. Amity went 15 seasons without reaching the SCC final. It has now reached the championship game three times this decade. The Spartans' only loss this season was 2-1 at Glastonbury, which won the CCC championship and is still undefeated. "That's 20-plus goals we lost this year (without Kershnar) and we had to find a way to make it and we did," said Quigley, pointing out that Amity has 14 shutouts this season. "Our defense is really, really good." Tea Bocek had two goals and an assist for the Spartans, who led 3-0 at halftime. Hand (11-5-3) struggled some toward the end of the regular season, but was able to pull off two upsets in the SCC tournament, beating No. 2 Notre Dame-West Haven and No. 3 Cheshire - both on the road and both shutouts - to reach Wednesday's championship game. But the Tigers couldn't stop the Spartans. Now, Amity, the No. 7 seed, will try to return to the Class LL championship game for a second consecutive season. They fell to Greenwich last year. The Spartans could face Mercy for a fourth time in a second-round home game. Glastonbury, Ridgefield and Trumbull are also in Amity's half of the draw. item.description: UNITED STATES - OCTOBER 21: Yerlin Confidan #55 of the Peoria Javelinas signs autographs for fans prior to the game between the Desert Dogs and the Javelinas at Peoria Sports Complex on Wednesday, October 21, 2026 in Peoria, AZ United States. (Photo by Jill Weisleder/Minor League Baseball via Getty Images) The Cincinnati Reds once again find themselves as a provider of players for the Peoria Javelinas in this year’s Arizona Fall League. While not all of the work has come at their farm system’s expense, the Javelinas do find themselves atop the six-team standings at 14-10 at the moment, and that’s where they stood when the participants in Sunday’s AFL Fall Star Game were announced. Three prospects off the Cincinnati farm were included on the roster for the National League side, including promising powerful young outfielder Yerlin Confidan. He sits tied for 10th in the league with 20 hits to his name to date, and he’s hitting .339/.371/.627 (.998 OPS) through 59 PA in what’s become a showcase for his toolsy repertoire. He’s also going to participate in the AFL Home Run Derby on Saturday. Joining Confidan is infielder Carlos Sanchez, who’s having an equally impressive run of form in AFL play so far. Through 17 games (58 PA) he has walked as many times (14) as he has struck out (14), and has popped 4 homers in route to a .259/.397/.534 line. Considering he’s still just 21 and mowed through High-A Dayton to the tune of .313/.409/.504 (.912 OPS) in 325 PA before a mid-season promotion to AA Chattanooga, I’m more and more believing the Reds may be on to something with him. Righty Luke Holman is having his own breakout in AFL play so far. The oft-injured former 2nd round pick out of LSU has been stellar so far through 13.0 IP (5 G), allowing just a lone earned run while fanning 20 against just 7 walks. It’s great to see him not only back healthy, but also shining given a) his journey through surgeries and recoveries since being drafted in 2024 and b) how thin the pitching depth in the Reds system has become of late. item.title: Ex-Michigan Coach Sends Strong Message to Ryan Day After Ohio State Gets Overlooked by CFP Committee
item.description: Ohio State head coach ©IMAGO/Newscom World Ohio State has managed to find an unlikely supporter in the middle of its latest College Football Playoff controversy. Former Michigan coach Biff Poggi isn’t buying the committee’s decision to leave the Buckeyes sitting at No. 12 in its first CFP rankings. For him, the problem is what the committee appears to be telling teams about scheduling tough opponents and taking risks. Speaking on the Big Ten Network , Biff Poggi questioned how Ohio State could be punished for accepting one of the toughest nonconference challenges on its schedule. He also had a pointed suggestion for Ryan Day. “Everybody’s been saying, ‘Oh, the committee always says, well, strength of schedule,’” he said. “Ohio State lays everything on the line, everything on the line. Week two, they go to Texas. They lose the game, but they play great at Texas. They’re getting absolutely hammered for playing that game.” That’s what bothered him. Ohio State went on the road to face Texas, took the risk, and now finds itself outside the projected playoff field. The CFP snub has ignited a firestorm. Get insider analysis on what it means for Ohio State's playoff hopes and the debate reshaping college football's selection process. Credits: IMAGO Biff Poggi knows the Michigan side of the rivalry well. He worked under Jim Harbaugh as associate head coach during the Wolverines’ successful 2021 and 2022 campaigns, both of which ended with Big Ten championships and playoff appearances. He later returned to Michigan in 2025, eventually taking over as interim head coach before leaving after the Citrus Bowl. So seeing him defend Ohio State carries a little extra weight. His argument goes beyond the Texas defeat. Ohio State also had to deal with the loss of starting QB Julian Sayin, a former Heisman finalist, before their matchup with USC. Backup Luke Fahey stepped into the lineup, but the Buckeyes struggled and suffered a 30-18 defeat. Biff Poggi acknowledged that the performance wasn’t good. What he couldn’t understand was the committee seemingly allowing one game without Julian Sayin to overshadow the larger picture. “They don’t play great against USC,” he said. “But to have them not in the conversation because you’re right, Rick, they’re the first out. If this thing’s played tomorrow, they’re not playing for it. And I think that is, you’ve got one of the league’s very best football teams, and what might be the best league in the country, and they’re not even in it. To me, it’s mind-blowing, and I think it’s wrong.” Biff Poggi’s frustration isn’t isolated, either. Paul Finebaum, who has rarely been shy about criticizing Ohio State, also sided with the Buckeyes during an appearance on ESPN’s Get Up . “They went to Texas, Greeney, on the second week of the season,” he said. “That’s what you’re supposed to do in college football. Indiana doesn’t do that, most schools don’t, but they did, and they got completely robbed as a result. This committee is a disgrace.
